prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (2010 manifesto)

Tax, benefits, and public finances
- Raise the personal income tax allowance to £10,000, taking low earners out of tax; fund via restricting higher-rate pension tax relief, aligning capital gains with income tax rates, anti-avoidance measures, a 1% levy on property value above £2m, and replacing Air Passenger Duty with a per‑plane duty (with a higher domestic rate where alternatives exist).
- Restore the state pension link to earnings (with a floor) and end compulsory annuitisation at 75; reform winter fuel support; simplify tax credits.
- Identify multi‑year savings (e.g., public sector pay cap of £400 for two years, restrict tax credits, end Child Trust Fund payments, Banking Levy, scrap ID cards/biometric passports, cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B, prison reform, reduce central bureaucracy) and conduct a cross‑government spending review. Consider alternatives to like‑for‑like Trident replacement and review public sector pensions.
- Establish a Council on Financial Stability and hold an emergency budget to begin changes from 2011–12.

Economy, banking, and jobs
- Separate retail and investment banking; curb bonus structures; use public stakes to restart lending.
- Create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges; reform takeover rules and business rates (site value basis, local control); reduce regulatory burden (one‑in, one‑out; end “gold‑plating” of EU rules).
- One‑year green stimulus to create c.100,000 jobs: offshore wind supply chain investment, eco cashback for home upgrades, energy upgrades for public buildings and schools, bring 250,000 empty homes into use, bus scrappage. Large youth work‑placement scheme; expand foundation degrees and adult apprenticeships.
- Establish a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for energy and transport.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn “pupil premium” for disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes, fund one‑to‑one support, SEN assessment at age 5, improved teacher training, anti‑bullying measures.
- Independent standards authority; slimmed curriculum; reduce high‑stakes testing; create a General Diploma spanning academic/vocational routes; college options at 14–19; better FE/6th‑form funding parity; reformed league tables.
- Limit ministerial micromanagement; locally commissioned “sponsor‑managed schools” with inclusive admissions; pay flexibility.
- Phase out undergraduate tuition fees over six years (final‑year fees scrapped immediately); national bursaries; refocus adult skills funding.

Health and care
- Protect frontline services by cutting management costs and quangos; prioritise prevention; integrate health and social care; guaranteed respite for carers; expand talking therapies; target alcohol harm; cut air pollution.
- Patient entitlements on waiting times (with NHS‑funded alternatives if missed); elected local health boards; free GP choice and email access; extra support for practices in high‑need areas; transparency on medical errors; language/competence tests.

Families, work, and consumers
- Shared parental leave (with scope to extend); flexible working for all; statutory youth services; default child contact arrangements where safe.
- Pay audits and name‑blind recruitment in larger firms; stronger disability employment support.
- Energy tariff reform (cheapest initial block), social tariffs and off‑grid support; tackle unfair bank charges; PostBank; cap credit/store card interest; clearer airline pricing; rail fare cuts and compensation; parking reforms.

Climate, environment, transport, and housing
- Net‑zero by 2050; >40% emissions cut by 2020; at least 40% power from non‑carbon sources by 2020 (rising to 100% by 2050); renewables roadmap, grid upgrades, European supergrid; block unabated coal; oppose new nuclear; strengthen efficiency targets.
- EU leadership on a tighter ETS, 30% 2020 target, tech transfer, HFC curbs; fund adaptation via international markets.
- Zero‑waste strategy; biodiversity recovery by 2020; protect greenfield; expand access to the countryside; localised planning with third‑party appeal; double woodland by 2050; water management reforms.
- Shift investment from roads to rail; regulated fares cut (RPI‑1%); reform Network Rail; empower councils over buses; cycling/walking promotion; per‑plane duty; cancel Heathrow expansion; prepare revenue‑neutral road pricing; rural fuel discount.
- Prevent repossessions where possible; insulate homes nationally; tighter building regs; enable council housebuilding; scrap HIPs (retain EPCs).

Crime, justice, immigration, and asylum
- 3,000 additional police; reduce police bureaucracy; elected police authorities with stronger powers; National Crime Reduction Agency; data‑led hotspot policing; evidence‑based drugs policy focused on treatment.
- Presumption against prison terms under six months; offender work and victim compensation; expand restorative justice; move addicts/mentally ill to secure treatment; cancel new prison programme.
- Reintroduce exit checks; create a National Border Force; regional points‑based work system; enforce against rogue employers; prioritise deporting serious offenders; earned citizenship for long‑term residents meeting criteria (pre‑2010 arrivals).
- Independent asylum agency; coordinated EU system; right to work; end child detention; safe‑return safeguards and alternatives to detention.

Governance, devolution, and civil liberties
- Proportional voting (STV) with fewer MPs; votes at 16; fixed terms; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; fully elected second chamber; written constitution via citizens’ convention and referendum; recall MPs; donation cap; lobbying register and rules; extend FOI; decentralise taxation/powers to local government; implement further devolution and a needs‑based funding formula.
- Freedom Bill: regulate CCTV and surveillance; reform extradition; protect jury trial and protest rights; libel reform; scrap ID cards/biometric passports; limit new offences; end blanket communications data retention; remove innocent DNA; uphold the Human Rights Act; scrap ContactPoint.

Foreign policy, defence, and development
- Strategic Security and Defence Review; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; no like‑for‑like Trident replacement; strengthen European defence cooperation; improve pay/housing for lower ranks; reduce MoD overheads.
- Use EU influence on major international issues; Afghanistan strategy tied to governance and regional diplomacy, aiming to enable troop withdrawal during the next Parliament; support for an Arms Trade Treaty and cluster‑munitions ban; diplomatic approach on Iran (oppose military action); inquiry into torture/rendition; two‑state approach in the Middle East and end to the Gaza blockade.
- Enshrine 0.7% GNI aid by 2013; new finance (e.g., transaction taxes), IFI reform, anti‑corruption and tax‑haven measures; climate finance additional to aid; focus on health, education, water; debt cancellation and action on vulture funds.
